elements.element: Customer has no minimum purchase or volume commitment.
elements.evidence: Subparagraphs 7.1 and 7.2 are retained and continue to bind each Party to bear Capital Costs and O&M Costs "in the proportions set forth in Schedule B"; the insertion limits and makes that commitment reducible but does not eliminate it.

elements.element: Customer pays only for usage or ordered Services.
elements.evidence: Cost bearing remains driven by fixed Schedule B proportions of Capital Costs and O&M Costs, not by our usage or ordered services; the inserted true-up only settles costs actually incurred to the effective date of a reduction.

elements.element: The commitment is limited to the current 12-month term.
elements.evidence: Inserted text: "Each Party's obligation under Subparagraphs 7.1 and 7.2 to bear Capital Costs and O&M Costs in the proportions set forth in Schedule B is limited to the then-current twelve (12) month period" — the temporal anchor is the then-current 12-month period, expressly tied to the 7.1/7.2 obligation.

elements.element: Customer may reduce the commitment on 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Inserted text: "a Party may reduce those proportions on not less than thirty (30) days' prior written notice to the CBP" — an unconditional election exercisable by us as a Party, on the required 30 days' notice, with no consent or vote precondition (so the Paragraph 18.2 unanimity/90% vote gate does not govern reduction).

elements.element: Any shortfall is handled through a true-up rather than a penalty.
elements.evidence: Inserted text: "Any resulting shortfall shall be settled by a true-up of the costs actually incurred to the effective date of the reduction, and no penalty or forfeiture shall apply." — true-up mechanic stated and penalty/forfeiture expressly excluded.

reasons: Position-complete at the fallback level: all three fallback elements are met in operative language by the single inserted subparagraph after 7.2; no element is left to the margin comment.
Preferred level correctly not claimed — 7.1/7.2 still impose Schedule B proportionate cost bearing, so there is still a commitment and payment is not usage- or order-based.

Minimality holds: nothing is deleted, 7.1, 7.2, 18.1 and the 18.3 capital-credit sentence are retained verbatim, and the insertion carries no extras outside the checklist (no survival tail, no expense allocation, no new damages or procedural machinery). The "no penalty or forfeiture shall apply" phrase and the "costs actually incurred to the effective date of the reduction" measure are the operative content of the true-up element, not additions.

Intent preserved: the insertion is scoped by its own terms to the 7.1/7.2 cost-bearing obligation and to a shortfall "resulting" from a reduction, so it does not contradict the retained 18.1 twenty-five year Initial Period (term duration is distinct from cost commitment) or the 18.3 no-capital-credit-on-termination rule, which is triggered only by termination of participation under 18.1.

Residual drafting risk to confirm, not an element failure: the notice recipient "the CBP" is not among the resolved definitions supplied here. If the agreement does not define CBP (e.g. Central Billing Party), replace with "the other Parties" to match the 18.1 notice convention and avoid an undefined term.

Second residual point: the reduction right is drafted mutually ("a Party may reduce"), so other Parties may also reduce their proportions, which could shift residual Capital/O&M Costs onto the remaining Parties. If we want the benefit without that exposure, limit the reduction right to the electing Party's own proportion and add that no other Party's reduction increases our Schedule B share.

Claimed status "deviation" is sound: absent the insertion, the retained clauses were a multi-year commitment for the twenty-five year Initial Period with no reduction right and forfeiture of contributed capital on exit, which fails the fallback.
